idea-plugin.name: Firestore Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Browse Firestore collections, documents, and subcollections in a tool window, authenticating with a GCP service account key -- entirely local REST calls, no gRPC/heavy SDK dependency. A real paid competitor's reviewers reported, three separate times over 8+ months: "'Connection test failed: java.util.NoSuchElementException: Collection contains no element matching the predicate.'" -- an opaque error that says nothing about what's actually wrong. This plugin looks up every required service-account field explicitly and reports the exact missing or malformed field by name; there is no bare `.first {}`/`.single {}` anywhere in the auth path for that exception to come from.

Another cited complaint: "it works very poorly with sub-collections. I would like to see these sub-collections in tabular form as well, not just in JSON." The tool window lists each collection's documents in a real table, with a button to drill into a selected document's own subcollections. All network calls run off the EDT; the service account JSON's contents and the resulting access token are held in memory only, never logged or persisted -- only the file path and project ID are saved. Scalar fields (string, integer, double, boolean) are editable in place from the same table.

Firestore Companion Pro: saved project profiles to switch between dev/staging/prod service accounts without retyping both fields every time; a query/filter builder (field + operator + value) against Firestore's own :runQuery endpoint, instead of always listing an entire collection; and exporting a collection's documents to a pretty-printed JSON file for a quick local backup/debug snapshot, preserving int64 precision exactly as Firestore stores it.
